entries.title: Infant & Toddler Storytime
entries.description: Infant and Toddler Storytime invites children and their caregivers to wiggle, rhyme, and sing with diverse books, songs, and fingerplays that encourage language, play, and exploration.\nThis program is geared for children 0 to 3 years of age and their parents/caregivers, but all children are welcome!

entries.title: Playdates for Children and Their Caregivers
entries.description: Kids get to practice early social skills like sharing, taking turns, imitation of play, and joint attentionnbsp;while caregivers get a chance to connect. \nDon't miss out on this chance to celebrate the joys of play while connecting with other families in the community.

entries.title: Reading to Children
entries.description: Participating in the Reading to Childrennbsp;program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning.nbsp;\nChildren will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer and it will be held under the Read to Children sign, within the Children's Area.\nFree.

entries.title: Game On!
entries.description: Our Nintendo Switch console is available for teens to play after school.nbsp; Controllers and games may be checked out at the Information Desk for IN LIBRARY USE ONLY.nbsp;nbsp;For teens 13-18.

entries.title: Lego Engineering
entries.description: Build, learn and imagine with Lego!

entries.title: Crochet Club
entries.description: A casual beginner friendly introduction to crocheting.

entries.title: Edenvale Teens Reach Meeting
entries.description: Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates.

entries.title: Everyone Can Create: Drawing with Sketchbook
entries.description: We will explore creative tools and techniques using the popular Sketchbook app.\nWe will learn to use Sketchbook, a beginner drawing app for the iPad.

entries.title: Reading Buddy in English & Spanish
entries.description: Children in kindergartennbsp;through 3rd grade are invited to read aloud in English ornbsp;Spanish to trained teen volunteers who will offer encouragement and help with pronunciation when needed.

entries.title: Safe Routes to School Working Group Meetings for 2026-27
entries.description: Working Group meetings bring together these partners to discuss how to further the program's mission: to make it safer for students and families in Cupertino to get to and from school actively.

entries.title: Wacky Wednesdays: Litterbug craft
entries.description: Each week we focus on a different themed artwork or craft.

entries.title: Afterschool Stories and Craft
entries.description: Join us for a fun afternoon of stories and craft for children ages 5-8 years in the picture book area.

entries.title: Personal Insight Questions (PIQs) Writing Workshop
entries.description: Work one-on-one with an experienced writing instructor who will help you craft and revise your PIQs that avoid common mistakes and showcase the best of who you are to the admissions team.

entries.title: VIRTUAL Math Olympiad Club
entries.description: nbsp;All sessions will be held online using Zoom.\nChildrennbsp;ages 8-11nbsp;will learn how to solve difficult math problems as preparation for the MOEMSnbsp;math competition in middle school.

entries.title: Knitting/Crocheting/Tatting/Bobbin Lace Club
entries.description: Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts?

entries.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines
entries.description: Join your community to helpnbsp;beautify your Edenvale Branch Library.

entries.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines as a Branch Buddy
entries.description:
Volunteer Away Your Fines at 20 per hour and earn community service hours while helping the library maintain a clean and welcoming environment.nbsp;
Volunteers may be asked to assist with:
Cleaning materials, bookshelves, furniture, and computersChildren's toys cleanup
Details and Requirements:
Must be able to commit to the 60-minute sessionAnyone under the age of 15 must volunteer alongside a parent/guardianNo experience or special skills necessaryThe library will provide supplies
Space is limited.

entries.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines as a Holiday Decorator
entries.description:
Details and Requirements:
• Must be able to commit to the full 1-hour session
• Anyone under the age of 15 must volunteer alongside a parent/guardian
• No experience or special skills necessary.

entries.title: Bollywood Dance
entries.description: Join us for this exciting volunteer-led program and learn Bollywood Dance moves for fun and fitness!

entries.title: BYOB (Bring Your Own Book) Book Club
entries.description: Find a book that is funny, witty, or clever with themes such as dark humor, satire, or comedic reliefMay 20: Movie Adaptation May!

entries.title: Hindi for Everyday Life
entries.description: Perfectly tailored for learners from all backgrounds whether they hear Hindi at home or are exploring it for the very first time.\n The curriculum nurtures the four core language skills - Speaking, Listening, Reading and Writing aligned with US Academic Standards andnbsp;the California World Languages Framework.

entries.title: Indoor Music and Movement
entries.description: nbsp;Music and Movement is a high energy Storytime - anbsp;fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning and movement.

entries.title: Teen Craft & Connect
entries.description: Teen Craft Connect (ages 12–18) is a welcoming weekly program created to help teens hang out, get creative, and build real connections in a friendly, relaxed setting.nbsp;\nOctober 7 - Trinket TraysOctober 14 - Tote BagsOctober 21 - Mini PumpkinsOctober 28 - Bedazzling\nFree supplies provided while they last.

entries.title: Reading to Children
entries.description: Participating in the Reading to Childrennbsp;program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning.nbsp;\nChildren will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer and it will be held under the Read to Children sign, within the Children's Area.\nFree.

entries.title: Baby Lapsit Storytime
entries.description: This program is for babies that are not yet walking confidently, and their caregivers. \nBaby Lapsit invites newborns, young infants,nbsp;and their caregivers to learn together and strengthen their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play.\nAfter Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay Play!

entries.title: Coffee and Blocks: Playdate for Children and Their Caregivers
entries.description: Kids will discover new toys and activities while adults will have a chance to chat and get acquainted while sipping coffee.

entries.title: Fuse Bead Crafternoon
entries.description: \nIn this workshop participants will create their own artwork using colorful fusion beads.

entries.title: STEM: DIY Abacus
entries.description: Construct your own abacus to practice mental calculations and arithmetic skills.This program is recommended for patrons 6 to 9 years old.No registration required; first-come, first-served; capacities limited.

entries.title: Autumn Trees!
entries.description: Join us for some Fall artnbsp;fun as we paint autumn trees!

entries.title: STEM Club: Modeling Asteroids
entries.description: This week in celebration of Native American Heritage Month, we'll learn aboutnbsp;Aaron Yazzie, a mechanical engineer who has worked onnbsp;Mars Science Laboratory, InSight, and Mars 2020 missions.

entries.title: Create Your Own Marble Maze!
entries.description: nbsp; In this hands-on workshop, you will design and create a marble maze.nbsp; We will teach you how to experiment with different designs to decide what works best and harness your artistic side for creative solutions and decorating your creation.nbsp; At the end, you take home your very own marble maze!

entries.title: Kids' Writing Club
entries.description: Children will learn how to express themselves throughnbsp;writing stories and practical writing tasks like letters and thank you notes.nbsp; Our fall schedule is:September: How to Write a StoryOctober: Spooky StoryNovember: Thank-you LetterDecember: Letter to SantaJanuary: Plot and Three Little PigsThrough different writing assignments students will learn about their own voice and become more effective communicators.

entries.title: Native American Heritage Month Storytime
entries.description: Join us for a special storytime as we celebrate and learn about Native American Heritage Month through stories, songs, and more of your favorite storytime activities.\nThis program is in celebration of Native American Heritage Month.\nFree.

entries.title: Thanksgiving Storytime and Craft
entries.description: Listen to stories and sing songs that celebrate family, thankfulness, and togetherness.

entries.title: Wee Love Art: Fall Leaf Sensory Painting in Baggies
entries.description: Children will putnbsp;leaf-shaped cardstock into a ziplocnbsp;bag and choose fall colors to add in, mixingnbsp;the paint within the closed ziploc bag.

entries.title: *Virtual * East Carnegie Teens Reach Meeting
entries.description: To join Teens Reach you must be 13-18 years of age, have a strong interest in the library, enjoy working with people of all ages and cultures, be reliable and communicative, and be willing to learn new skills.

entries.title: Pearl Avenue Teens Reach Meeting
entries.description: Our in-person meet up plans include: Teen Volunteer Opportunities Election for Advisory Board Community Youth Engagement Games & Activities Snacks Guest Speakers Bring a friend, and learn more about what to expect with volunteering this year.

entries.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines - Vineland
entries.description: Join us at the Vineland Branch Library!

entries.title: Third Thursdays with Poetry Center San Jose
entries.description: He's a speaker on the LGBT speaker's bureau and loves using his art to spread Black queer joy.Open mic to follow.\nPoetry Center San José's mission is to nurture and promote diverse literary expression in our community as a means of exploring, defining, and enriching the human experience.For those under 18 years of age who may be attending, we recommend that a parent/legal guardian be with you during the program.Free.

entries.description: nbsp;Baby Lapsit invites newborns, infants, babies, and their caregivers to learn together and strengthen their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play.After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay Play.
